{"id": "2:282/q19", "question": "May a scribe charge for writing?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:282/q19/p1", "position": "Payment for a scribe depends on the legal status and burden of the work.", "reasons": "TAB-FULL (مجاهد): Mujāhid says a requester harms a busy scribe or witness by insisting “fear God, you were commanded” when other people can be found; they need not interrupt their work or feel pressured. ZAJJAJ (الشاعر): An unnamed poet uses داينت ليلى for dealing with Layla in debts, then describes delay in repayment and partial payment. TABRISI (الجبائي): Al-Jubbāʾī allows a scribe and witness to take payment, while al-Ṭūsī says their school does not permit it; paper costs belong to the creditor. QURTUBI-FULL (ابن العربي): He says the command is guidance, so the writer need not write before being paid. QURTUBI-FULL (الربيع والضحاك): They say the order to write was abrogated by the prohibition against harming a writer or witness; al-Qurṭubī calls this remote because a universal obligation was never established and paid document-writing is permitted. QURTUBI-FULL (author): Scholars agree valid salam specifies described, commonly available food, measure, term, payment in known currency before the parties separate, and delivery place; he knows no scholar who invalidates such a contract. BAYDAWI-FULL (author): Lā yuḍārr has two readings: scribes and witnesses must not refuse, distort, or alter testimony, or others must not harm them by disrupting duties, demanding extra travel, or withholding their fees and expenses. NASAFI-FULL (author): The active reading forbids a scribe or witness to refuse, distort, add, or omit; the passive forbids burdening them, rushing them from duties, withholding the scribe's fee, or making a witness bear travel costs. BIQAI-FULL (أبو الحسن الحرالي): Al-Harali says the verse encourages kindness to scribes and witnesses and permits compensation when their work would otherwise damage their livelihood. BURSEVI (author): If active, the prohibition bars a scribe from refusing or altering the document and a witness from withholding testimony; if passive, it bars others from harming them while occupied or withholding their fee. ALUSI-FULL (author): If active, the verse forbids witnesses and scribes to refuse, distort, add, or subtract; if passive, it forbids burdening them, withholding the fee, or requiring costly travel. ALUSI-FULL (author): Some take saʾama as laziness by euphemism, since the Qurʾan describes hypocrites as praying lazily; a hadith says a believer should say prayer feels burdensome, not lazy. | mentions 4:142 ELMALILI (author): Alternatively, on the passive reading, scribes and witnesses themselves must not be harmed by excessive demands, interruption of important work, or denial of a scribe’s fee. KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): Whether a scribe may charge depends on whether writing is obligatory, since religious duties cannot be paid work but optional acts may be; the author deems abstention impermissible when capable writers are available, especially if no substitute exists and rights may be lost.
